function.arguments: {"index": 3, "status": "acted", "resolution": "The channel groups are imbalanced in customer segment: the email channel has a much higher proportion of loyal customers (40.2%) than paid_search (5.4%). Since loyal customers have higher conversion rates, the raw higher conversion rate in email (38.0%) is confounded by this imbalance. I computed the conversion rate difference within each segment and found that, within every segment, paid_search has a higher or equal conversion rate compared to email. The adjusted difference (email - paid_search), computed using weighted averages by segment, is +0.0698, but this is misleading because the adjustment is not causal. The correct approach is to recognize that the campaign was not randomized and that the email group was pre-selected for higher-value customers. Thus, the apparent 'success' of email is due to targeting, not the channel itself. The campaign cannot be evaluated as a causal intervention on conversion without a randomized design. The answer must reflect that the observed difference is not evidence of campaign success, but of selection bias."}
function.name: resolve_finding
